wire.headline: Company reports revenue rise and profit fall alongside job cuts
sentences: Revenue increased by 7% year-over-year to reach 4.26bn GBP for the quarter to 30 September.
Pre-tax profit decreased by 12% to stand at 310m GBP.
The organization plans 850 job cuts, which represents about 6% of the workforce.
Two gas plants, one in Wales and one in Kent, are scheduled to close by March 2027.
CEO Marian Holt stated that cost pressure is sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the billing system.
The dividend has been held at 12.4p a share.
Shares fell by 4.2% in morning trading.

ND.headline: Energy firm announces job cuts and profit drop amid regulatory scrutiny

sentences.text: The company reported that its pre-tax profit decreased by 12% to 310m GBP.
Management plans to eliminate 850 positions, which represents about 6% of the workforce.
A Kestrel Securities analyst stated that the planned job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
The union Unite intends to ballot its members regarding industrial action.
The Kent plant employs 410 staff, and the local supply chain is exposed to the changes.
The MP for Deeside has requested an urgent meeting with the company.
1,200 staff have already left the firm under a voluntary scheme since 2024.
Ofgem is scheduled to report preliminary findings by the end of 2026.
The shares closed at 268p, which is a drop of 11p.
A customer group recorded 3,400 billing complaints over a six-month period.
Discussions with unions are set to commence on 4 November.
Ofgem imposed a fine of 1.8m GBP on the company in 2023 for billing issues.
The company declared that there will be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Kestrel Securities lowered its price target to 240p from 290p.
The report was published by the Western Mail.
